questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Identify the audience of a design brief
questions.stem: In a bridge retrofit brief, who is the primary audience the engineer must address first?

options.text: The structural review board with authority over safety
The city council that approves funding and permits
options.misconception: treats a secondary stakeholder as primary

options.text: The general public who will walk across the bridge
options.misconception: confuses end users with decision makers

options.text: The contractor who will pour the concrete

questions.explanation: The review board holds safety authority, so it is the primary audience. End users and contractors matter but do not decide approval.
questions.hint: Ask who can say no to the design.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a claim needs support
questions.stem: Why does an engineer's load-bearing claim need evidence beyond the design brief?

answer.exemplar: A claim without evidence is only an assertion; the review board needs data, calculations, and standards citations to trust that the structure will perform as promised under load.

questions.explanation: Unsupported claims fail review because reviewers cannot verify safety. Evidence turns an assertion into a defensible engineering position.
questions.hint: Think about what a reviewer must verify.
